title: Cedarglen QA integration scratchbook
content:
Context / meeting: quick intake w/ Cedarglen QA (Nov 18) to capture constraints for their retail checkout assistant pilot. They want a small on-prem/private deployment behind a strict VPC and regional egress restrictions. Primary ask: low-latency interactive responses for agent-assisted QA flows (90th percentile < 120ms for short chat prompts) and complete auditability for each inference request.

Attendees: Cedarglen: Aaron Park (SRE), Lina Gomez (QA lead); Redwood: Maya Chen (SE), Rafael Ortiz (Infra).

High-level customer constraints (notes):
- Must run in customer VPC with no public internet egress from inference hosts (control plane allowed to communicate to a management endpoint over a whitelisted IP range).
- KMS integration for key wrapping; they will provide AWS KMS with restricted IAM roles.
- Data retention policy: logs must be retained for 365 days; audit logs must be exportable to their SIEM (Splunk).
- Cannot use third-party telemetry: no usage telemetry leaves VPC except aggregated billing metrics via the control plane using a dedicated endpoint.

Technical gotchas / quick flag list:
- Model size: they prefer a 7B quantized LLM for cost, but their peak concurrency (~40 agents) suggests dedicated pooling + batching. Need to surface tokenization/response time tradeoffs per model in the proposal.
- KV cache persistence: they want session affinity so repeated short-turn prompts don’t re-tokenize repeatedly. Will need to confirm cache eviction policy (suggest LRU per session + optional persistent cache volume).
- Network latency constraint for on-prem edge: their east-coast datacenter has variable intra-region jitter — recommend co-locating a small serving pool in that AZ.
- Function calling: they will call internal product APIs for price lookup. Must ensure function call payloads are only routed to their internal API gateway (no outbound to hosted endpoints).

Security / compliance notes:
- Bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via AWS KMS; confirm HSM requirement (they asked about HSM-backed CMKs). Follow up: is HSM mandatory for production?
- Audit requirements: every inference must include a request_id, user_id, route, model_version. Plan to add a lightweight logging hook that writes to local S3-compatible store and forwards to Splunk via their collector.

Performance targets and measurement plan:
- Target: 90th perc generation latency < 120ms for 32-token responses, p95 < 250ms for 128-token responses.
- Measurement: run synthetic replay of 1k concurrent short-turn sessions; measure token throughput and 90/95 latencies; attach traces from our agent and their network.
- Cost target: under $0.008/token assumed for 7B quantized when amortized across sustained throughput — rough ballpark, will refine after bench runs.

Operational model / rollout suggestions:
1) PoC: 1 small serving lane (2x A100-sim equivalent or 4x T4s depending on availability) + prefix caching enabled, session affinity, limited to 10 agents. 2-week run.
2) Scale: add dedicated GPU pool and autoscaling policy with burst capacity. Canary a model variant: quantized 7B -> 6-bit / int4 tuning -> monitor evals.
3) SLA: propose 99.5% uptime for serving nodes; support window 9am-6pm PST with oncall escalation.

Open questions (action items):
- Aaron to confirm whether HSM is mandatory or optional (due: 2026-03-05).
- Cedarglen to provide a sanitized sample prompt set (1000 short-turn examples) for quality benchmarking (due: 2025-12-01).
- Rafael to validate we can expose a management endpoint over their allowed IP CIDR and confirm port restrictions (due: 2025-11-25).
- Maya to produce a quick cost sketch with 7B quantized vs 13B int8 variants and tradeoffs (ETA: next Tues).

Next steps (internal):
- Draft one-page technical proposal + deployment diagram (include VPC flow, KMS binding, logging path) -> assign to Maya (draft by 2025-11-22).
- Run internal bench (local env) with 7B quantized image using a 40-concurrency replay to capture baseline latency numbers (Rafael, 2025-11-24).
- Open JIRA epic JIRA-CED-321 and link this doc; create stories for KMS onboarding, cache persistence, and Splunk exporter.

Random capture / quick wins:
- Could use prefix cache warmers during business hours to reduce cold-gen spikes for frequent SKUs.
- Consider a lightweight token-budget limiter per session to cap runaway costs.
- Recommend a short runbook doc for Cedarglen SRE on diagnosing spike sources (network vs serving runtime).

Tone: keep this doc informal; it’s our scratchbook for the intake. Will formalize into a proposal after the sample prompts arrive.

---
Raw snippets from call (verbatim):
"we can’t allow any outbound to third parties — even analytics vendors" — Aaron
"we want interactive feel — the team will escalate if human agents see >200ms delay" — Lina
"we can try int8 but if quality drops we'd fallback to 7B quantized in canary" — Maya

End of capture.
